newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil sugar export tax exemption still unsigned.
newsitem.headline: Brazil sugar export tax exemption still unsigned.

text.p: Tax exemption for an extra 500,000 tonnes of Brazilian sugar exports is still awaiting Finance Minister Pedro Malan's signature, officials said.
"There are a lot of papers that have to be signed (by the minister). It's (the sugar export tax exemption) is in the queue," said an aide to the minister.
The Ministry of Industry and Commerce passed to the Finance Ministry early this month a decree authorizing tax exemption for additional sugar exports.
The extra sales were themselves authorized in a decree published in the government's Official Journal in December.
The 500,000 tonnes are in addition to the 5.2 million tonnes of exports orginally set in the 1996/97 sugar crop plan.

Traders note that the additional export quota will have little immediate effect because most mills have no produce left to ship. They say they are likely to either sell their quotas to other mills or use them for the next crop.
